mustMemoriseRules: greenhouse gases → gases including carbon dioxide, methane and water vapour that absorb and emit infrared radiation
incoming solar radiation → short-wave radiation passing through the atmosphere relatively easily and warming Earth's surface
outgoing terrestrial radiation → long-wave infrared radiation emitted by the warmed Earth
greenhouse mechanism → absorption and re-emission of infrared radiation in all directions, reducing energy escape to space
human carbon dioxide sources → fossil-fuel burning and deforestation or other land-use change
human methane sources → cattle or rice agriculture and decomposition of landfill waste
sea-level consequence → a possible climate-change effect involving rising average sea level
rainfall consequence → changes in rainfall patterns caused by climate change
species-distribution consequence → organisms becoming more or less common in regions as climate changes
carbon footprint → total greenhouse-gas emissions over a full life cycle, usually expressed as carbon-dioxide equivalent
